There's **no official Xcode extension** for Claude Code yet (unlike VS Code and JetBrains which have direct integrations).

Here's how people use Claude Code with Xcode:

### Best approach: Terminal side-by-side

You're already doing it! Run Claude Code in a terminal pointed at your project directory, and keep Xcode open for building/running:

```
Terminal (Claude Code)          Xcode
├─ Read/edit Swift files        ├─ Build & run
├─ Refactor code                ├─ Debug
├─ Fix bugs                     ├─ Interface Builder
└─ Search codebase              └─ Simulator
```

Changes Claude makes to `.swift` files show up instantly in Xcode.

### Alternative: VS Code as a bridge

Some people open their Xcode project **also** in VS Code with the Claude Code extension installed. This gives you a chat-style UI while still using Xcode for builds/simulator. VS Code handles Swift syntax fine for editing.

### Tips for your current workflow

- Keep this terminal session open alongside Xcode
- When Claude edits a file, Xcode auto-detects the change and prompts to reload
- Use Claude for the code changes, Xcode for build/run/debug

That's really the workflow right now — there's no plugin that embeds Claude directly into Xcode's editor. If you want to request that feature, you can file it at https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues.

You were right! Claude is now **natively integrated into Xcode**. Here's how to set it up:

## Option 1: Xcode 26+ (Built-in Claude)

If you have **Xcode 26 or later**, Claude is built right in:

1. Open **Xcode > Settings > Accounts**
2. Sign in with your **Claude account** (requires Pro, Max, Team, or Enterprise plan)
3. Claude Sonnet 4 powers the coding assistant — you can interact with your code using natural language

## Option 2: Xcode 26.3 (Full Agentic Coding)

**Xcode 26.3** takes it further with the **Claude Agent SDK** integration:

- Full Claude Code power directly in Xcode (subagents, background tasks, plugins)
- Claude can capture **Xcode Previews** to see your UI and iterate on it
- Autonomous, long-running coding tasks
- MCP support so Claude Code CLI can also integrate with Xcode

### To update:
Check if you're on Xcode 26.3 — go to **Xcode > About Xcode**. If not, update via the Mac App Store or Apple Developer portal.

## Option 3: Claude Code CLI + MCP

Even from this terminal, you can connect to Xcode via MCP in 26.3 to capture Previews and interact with the IDE without leaving the CLI.

---

Check what version of Xcode you're running — from your screenshot it looks like it might be an older version. You may need to update to Xcode 26+ to get the Claude integration.
